❯ Without using any
  tools, write a
  1500-word essay on the
  history of the computer
  terminal, from
  teletypes to modern
  emulators.

───────────────────────────

  ⏸ plan mode on
  doubled as a crude
  storage device. It was
  loud and slow, and it
  cost far less than
  anything else that could
  talk to a computer. As a
  result it showed up
  everywhere, from
  university time-sharing
  systems to the first
  minicomputers.

  Time-sharing is what
  turned the teleprinter
  into a terminal. Systems
  such as MIT's Compatible
  Time-Sharing System
  (1961) and later Multics
  let many users share one
  computer at once, each at
  their own teleprinter,
  each apparently in sole
  control of the machine.
  The terminal became a
  window onto a shared
  resource, and the
  interactive command line
  was born.

  When Ken Thompson and
  Dennis Ritchie built Unix
  at Bell Labs around 1969
  to 1971, they worked on
  Teletype Model 33s and
  37s. That is why Unix
  commands are so short:
  ls, cp, rm, cat. Every
  character cost time and
  paper. It is also why
  Unix calls a terminal
  device a "tty," and still
  does. The kernel's "line
  discipline" hand
  ⎿  Interrup· What should
